summary.text: Adriana Guzmán Fralick, a Republican Reno lawyer who has held several state and local government legal posts but never elected office, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of Nevada to Nicole Cannizzaro.
Endorsed by President Trump, she campaigned on tougher sentencing, drug enforcement, and election security.

paragraphs.text: Guzmán Fralick earned a B.A. from the University of Nevada, Reno and a J.D. from the UNLV Boyd School of Law.

She served as legal counsel to the Nevada Commission on Ethics, general counsel to former Gov. Jim Gibbons and assistant general counsel to the Public Utilities Commission, and chaired the Nevada Cannabis Compliance Board.
She also worked in the Carson City District Attorney's Office on civil matters and has not served as a criminal prosecutor.
Guzmán Fralick has her own law firm in Reno, focusing on personal injury and legal and political counsel, and has served as an attorney for state agencies including the Nevada Gaming Control Board.
Her only prior run for office was a 2012 State Board of Education race, in which she finished third of five.
She won the Republican nomination for attorney general in the June 9, 2026 primary, defeating Douglas County Commissioner Danny Tarkanian.
She received 41.4% of the vote to Nicole Cannizzaro's 56.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
